comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C52-C59 regarding optimization of brighter variants and spectroscopic characterization. Both evaluations find this work SUPPORTED as part of the technical development and refinement process.

Perfect agreement on claims C72-C79 regarding generalizability to other transporters. Both evaluations find this work SUPPORTED, demonstrating the utility and broad applicability of the sensor design strategy.

Strong disagreement on mechanistic interpretation (C83, C84, C88). OpenEval finds the conformational change model SUPPORTED by functional evidence, while peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, arguing that fluorescence changes could reflect protonation upon binding rather than conformational changes associated with transport.

Major disagreement on what the sensor reports. OpenEval finds claims C60-C65, C68 SUPPORTED, concluding fluorescence reports transport activity based on transport-deficient mutants and suppressor screen. Peer reviewers rate overlapping claims (C8, C9, C39, C42, C60-C65, C68) as UNCERTAIN, arguing the data does not differentiate substrate binding from transport.

Agreement on claims C43-C46 regarding concentration dependence and correlation between EC50 and Km. Both evaluations find this SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers explicitly note the signal 'nicely tracks the NH4+ transport activity as measured directly by voltage-clamp methods.'
Agreement on claims C47-C51 regarding selectivity for ammonium. Both evaluations find this SUPPORTED as part of the characterization showing the sensor tracks extracellular NH4+ concentration.
Agreement on claims C32-C37 regarding linker optimization. Both evaluations find this SUPPORTED as part of the technical development that reviewers describe as 'carefully done.'
Agreement on claims C27-C31 regarding insertion site selection and tolerance. Both evaluations find this SUPPORTED as part of the methodological development and optimization process.

Agreement on claims C38, C40, C41 regarding correlation between insertion position, transport activity, and fluorescence. Both evaluations find this SUPPORTED as part of the functional characterization of sensor variants.

Partial overlap on claim C7 (sensor development). OpenEval finds C7-C10 SUPPORTED as the central finding. Peer reviewers acknowledge C7 as SUPPORTED technical achievement but separately question the interpretation of what the sensor reports (see R2 peer result).

Disagreement on suppressor screen interpretation (C66-C68). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED as rigorous validation that fluorescence reports transport. Peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, noting it 'would require more information on binding and how this might be differentiated in the mutants.'

Disagreement on low-affinity variant (C69-C71). OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED as additional evidence of faithful reporting. Peer reviewers include these claims in their UNCERTAIN evaluation, questioning whether the data differentiates binding from transport.

Agreement on claim C10 regarding technological utility. Both evaluations find this SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers explicitly state 'these reporters represent an important technical advance' and 'may be quite valuable' despite their concerns about mechanistic interpretation.

OpenEval finds background and context claims (C1-C6, C14, C16-C26) SUPPORTED by appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers focused on experimental claims rather than background literature.
OpenEval finds methodological context claims (C11-C13, C15) SUPPORTED by appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these represent established background information.

OpenEval finds structural background claims (C85-C87) SUPPORTED by citations to prior studies. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these represent established structural knowledge used for context.

OpenEval rates future applications (C89-C90) as UNCERTAIN since they represent untested proposals. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers do acknowledge potential utility in their discussion of C10.
